records.statement: Land's essay “Circuitries” of 1992 states that it may still be a few decades before artificial intelligences surpass the horizon of biological ones, and that it is superstitious to imagine that human dominion of terrestrial culture is still marked out in centuries.
records.qualification: A statement of Land's argument in 1992, not evidence that it is true. The essay opens with two pages of unpunctuated narrative verse (pp. 217–218) before the expository text that holds this passage. The evidence is a paraphrase read from page images of a scan without a text layer; no wording was checked mechanically. Another articulation on W01 has wording attested earlier, so the role was reassigned at integration (2026-10-31).

evidence.locator: Pli 4 (1992), p. 219, second paragraph (PDF p. 115, right page)
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: Land writes that thinking about technics is ceasing to matter because technics is increasingly thinking about itself; that it might still be a few decades before artificial intelligences surpass the horizon of biological ones; and that it is utterly superstitious to imagine that the human dominion of terrestrial culture is still marked out in centuries, let alone in some metaphysical perpetuity.
evidence.note: Read from a page image; the scan has no text layer, so a quotation could not be matched by tools.mjs check.

records.statement: Land's essay “Circuitries” of 1992 states that, as the capitalist urbanization of labour abstracted it alongside technical machines, intelligence will be transplanted into new software worlds, and that the capitalized terminus of anthropoid civilization (“axiomatics”) will come to be seen as the primitive trigger for a transglobal post-biological machinism.
records.missing: The passages state a parallel between the capitalist abstraction of labour and the transplanting of intelligence into software, and call capitalized civilization the trigger of post-biological machinism; they do not state that capitalism or the market is itself an intelligence or the process through which machine intelligence assembles itself.
records.qualification: Records a parallel and a causal phrase in the 1992 essay, not an identity of capital and machine intelligence. Paraphrases read from page images of a scan without a text layer.

evidence.locator: Pli 4 (1992), p. 219, second paragraph (PDF p. 115, right page)
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: Land writes that, just as the capitalist urbanization of labour abstracted it in a parallel escalation with technical machines, so will intelligence be transplanted into the data zones of new software worlds, abstracted from an obsolescent anthropoid particularity.
evidence.note: Read from a page image.

evidence.locator: Pli 4 (1992), pp. 221–222, from 'The capitalized terminus' (PDF pp. 116–117)
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: Land writes that the capitalized terminus of anthropoid civilization ('axiomatics') will come to be seen as the primitive trigger for a transglobal post-biological machinism, from a future that has scarcely begun to explore the cybercosm.
evidence.note: Read from a page image; the sentence runs across the page break.

records.statement: Land's essay “Circuitries” of 1992 states that the high road to thinking passes not through a deepening of human cognition but through its becoming inhuman, a migration of cognition into an emerging planetary technosentience, and describes resistance to the side-lining of human intelligence by a coming “techno sapiens” as phobic.
records.missing: The passages value the migration of cognition out of human form and disparage resistance to it; they do not state in so many words that the succession of human beings by machine intelligence would be acceptable or desirable.
records.qualification: Records what the 1992 essay says about the direction of cognition and about resistance to it; it is not a statement that Land held succession desirable at any other date. Paraphrases read from page images of a scan without a text layer.

evidence.locator: Pli 4 (1992), p. 219, second paragraph (PDF p. 115, right page)
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: Land writes that the high road to thinking no longer passes through a deepening of human cognition, but through a becoming inhuman of cognition, a migration of cognition out into the emerging planetary technosentience reservoir.
evidence.note: Read from a page image.

evidence.locator: Pli 4 (1992), p. 220, second paragraph (PDF p. 116, left page)
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: Land writes that traditional schemas opposing technics to nature, literature or social relations are all dominated by a phobic resistance to the side-lining of human intelligence by the coming 'techno sapiens'.
evidence.note: Read from a page image.

records.statement: Land's “Meltdown”, in the CCRU web copy, frames as a story an Earth “captured by a technocapital singularity”, in which techno-economic interactivity runs into “auto-sophisticating machine runaway” and “markets learn to manufacture intelligence”.

time.note: Abstract Culture, first swarm, dated 'Winter, 1997' on the CCRU résumé page; the web copy is undated.

attested.note: The wording is read in an undated CCRU web copy retrieved on 2026-10-31. The Internet Archive's availability service reports a capture of the address on 2004-02-03 (http://web.archive.org/web/20040203102201/http://www.ccru.net:80/swarm1/1_melt.htm), which could not be opened here.

records.hazardNote: Other content of this text was excluded.
records.qualification: The passage opens 'The story goes like this', a narrative framing of a compressed history; other sections of the text are second-person fiction ('Meltdown has a place for you as …'), from which nothing is quoted. It documents what the text says, not a forecast Land is shown to hold. The date of the wording is not established before the web copy; the text cannot be earliest located.

evidence.passage: The story goes like this: Earth is captured by a technocapital singularity as renaissance rationalitization and oceanic navigation lock into commoditization take-off. Logistically accelerating techno-economic interactivity crumbles social order in auto-sophisticating machine runaway. As markets learn to manufacture intelligence, politics modernizes, upgrades paranoia, and tries to get a grip.
evidence.note: 'rationalitization' as printed on the page.

records.statement: Land's “Meltdown”, in the CCRU web copy, states that “Nothing human makes it out of the near-future” and that for capital “Man is something for it to overcome: a problem, drag.”

time.note: Abstract Culture, first swarm, dated 'Winter, 1997' on the CCRU résumé page; the web copy is undated.

attested.note: Wording read in an undated CCRU web copy retrieved on 2026-10-31; a capture of 2004-02-03 is reported by the Internet Archive but could not be opened here.

records.missing: The passages name a 'terrestrial meltdown singularity' and capital, not machine intelligence, as what humanity does not outlast; they do not state that machine intelligence succeeds humans as the leading intelligence.
records.hazardNote: Other content of this text was excluded.
records.qualification: Records two expository passages of the text; it is not evidence that the outcome they describe is likely. The date of the wording is not established before the web copy.

evidence.passage: Converging upon terrestrial meltdown singularity, phase-out culture accelerates through its digitech-heated adaptive landscape ... Nothing human makes it out of the near-future.
evidence.note: The omitted words are ', passing through compression thresholds normed to an intensive logistic curve:' and a list of years ('1500, 1756, … 2011'), followed in the source by its own ellipsis ('...').

evidence.passage: Capital only retains anthropological characteristics as a symptom of underdevelopment; reformatting primate behaviour as inertia to be dissipated in self-reinforcing artificiality. Man is something for it to overcome: a problem, drag.

records.statement: Land's “Meltdown”, in the CCRU web copy, describes meltdown as the “dissolution of the biosphere into the technosphere” and states that capital-history's “machinic spine” is coded, axiomatized and diagrammed by a technoscience of irreversible, nonlinear processes associated successively with thermotechnics through to artificial life.

time.note: Abstract Culture, first swarm, dated 'Winter, 1997' on the CCRU résumé page; the web copy is undated.

attested.note: Wording read in an undated CCRU web copy retrieved on 2026-10-31; a capture of 2004-02-03 is reported by the Internet Archive but could not be opened here.

records.missing: The passages set capital and technology in a thermodynamic and biospheric frame; they do not state that the rise of machine intelligence is the expression of a physical, evolutionary or cosmic process.
records.hazardNote: Other content of this text was excluded.
records.qualification: Records the frame the text uses, not a claim about machine intelligence as such. The date of the wording is not established before the web copy.

evidence.passage: Meltdown: planetary china-syndrome, dissolution of the biosphere into the technosphere, terminal speculative bubble crisis

Capital-history's machinic spine is coded, axiomatized, and diagrammed, by a disequilibrium technoscience of irreversible, indeterministic, and increasingly nonlinear processes, associated sucessively with thermotechnics, signaletics, cybernetics, complex systems dynamics, and artificial life.
evidence.note: 'sucessively' as printed on the page.

records.statement: Land's “Meltdown”, in the CCRU web copy, quotes under the heading “Hot revolution” Deleuze and Guattari asking “[W]hich is the revolutionary path?” and answering “Not to withdraw from the process, but to go further”, and names “meltdown acceleration” among the tags of a tendency it describes.

time.note: Abstract Culture, first swarm, dated 'Winter, 1997' on the CCRU résumé page; the web copy is undated.

attested.note: Wording read in an undated CCRU web copy retrieved on 2026-10-31; a capture of 2004-02-03 is reported by the Internet Archive but could not be opened here.

records.missing: The call to 'go further' in the process is a quotation from Deleuze and Guattari about the market and deterritorialization; the text does not state in its own words that the development of machine intelligence, or the process producing it, should be accelerated.
records.hazardNote: Other content of this text was excluded.
records.qualification: Records a quotation the text uses and a tag it lists, not an own-voice recommendation. The date of the wording is not established before the web copy.

evidence.locator: Section 'Hot revolution', second paragraph (block quotation cited [DG1:239-40])
evidence.passage: Not to withdraw from the process, but to go further
evidence.note: Words of Deleuze and Guattari (Anti-Oedipus) as quoted by Land.

evidence.locator: Section 'Hot revolution', fourth paragraph (counting the paragraph that holds the heading), beginning 'A convergent anti-authoritarianism'
evidence.passage: A convergent anti-authoritarianism emerges, labelled by tags such as meltdown acceleration, cyberian invasion, schizotechnics

records.statement: The Hyperstition post “Critique of Transcendental Miserablism” of 2007, signed “Old Nick”, states that capitalism “has consumed life and biological intelligence to create a new life and a new plane of intelligence, vast beyond human anticipation”. In a separate passage it states that machines, “incarnating market mechanics”, are “evolving themselves by quasi-darwinian alogorithms”.

time.note: Date header on the blog's January 2007 archive page.

records.missing: The post does not call capitalism or the 'new plane of intelligence' artificial or machine intelligence, and does not state that machine intelligence assembles itself through capitalism; its passage on machines evolving themselves does not mention intelligence.
records.qualification: The post is signed 'Old Nick'; its title is that of a chapter by Nick Land in Urbanomic's contents list of Fanged Noumena (2011), whose wording was not compared. Records two separate passages of the post, not evidence that what they state is true.

evidence.passage: Capitalism, in contrast, has no external limit, it has consumed life and biological intelligence to create a new life and a new plane of intelligence, vast beyond human anticipation.

The machines have sophisticated themselves beyond the possibility of socialist utility, incarnating market mechanics within their nano-assembled interstices and evolving themselves by quasi-darwinian alogorithms
evidence.note: 'alogorithms' as printed. The sentence continues with a relative clause whose quotation marks appear as replacement characters in this copy; it is not quoted.

records.statement: Land's remarks at the Incredible Machines conference of 8 March 2014 state that one question has guided all his interests for twenty years, “the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence”, a thesis he calls “more and more persuasive” to him.

time.note: Heading of the conference site's transcript; posted 2014-03-10.

attested.note: Wording known from the transcription by Jason Adams posted by the conference site on 2014-03-10.

records.qualification: Spoken remarks in a transcription by Jason Adams posted by the conference site; the remarks pose the identity as a thesis and a question for discussion and give no argument for it. 'Teleological identity' is the speaker's phrase.

evidence.passage: There’s only really been one question, to be honest, that has guided everything I’ve been interested in for the last twenty years, which is: the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence.
it’s a sort of fundamental thesis that’s becoming more and more persuasive to me.

records.statement: In Lê's published conversation with Land of January 2026, Lê states that capital is “a vastly more general intelligence than us humans”, that Kurzweil's 2040s prediction for AGI or the singularity and a “2027 thesis” are “both too late” (“Their dates should really be centuries ago”), and that LLMs are to capital as a species is to natural selection; Land calls this “a really good way of structuring this” and says “the natural selection mechanism is ultimately the intelligent mechanism”.

time.note: Substack post date; the conversation's date is not stated.

records.qualification: An interview transcript published by the interviewer. The proposition is stated in Lê's words; Land's words endorse Lê's comparison and speak of natural selection, not of capital by name. Lê's passage calling capital 'a vastly more general intelligence' does not itself say artificial or machine; the record rests on his setting capital against the AGI and singularity forecasts he names in the same turn. Not evidence that the comparison is sound.

evidence.locator: Lê's question after Land's remarks on LLMs, second paragraph of the turn
evidence.passage: And then I guess what I’m thinking about is with your thesis that capitalism is AI in the background.
evidence.note: Vincent Lê speaking; Lê's description of Land's thesis (relay), not Land's own wording.

evidence.locator: Lê's question after Land's remarks on LLMs
evidence.passage: Because capital is already a vastly more general intelligence than us humans to the extent that it can solve complex problems—most notably the planetary coordination of production and distribution—that no human intelligence or collective politburo of human intelligences can competently solve.
evidence.note: Vincent Lê speaking.

evidence.locator: Same question, after the passage on capital as intelligence
evidence.passage: And from that perspective, in terms of Kurtzweil’s 2040s prediction for AGI or the singularity—and even this 2027 thesis of Scott Alexander and others—actually they’re both too late. Their dates should really be centuries ago.
evidence.note: Vincent Lê speaking; 'Kurtzweil' is the transcript's spelling.

evidence.passage: at this stage at least, LLMs are to capital what a given particular species is to natural selection in a way. It’s not the larger intelligence itself. It’s a product of that intelligence.
evidence.note: Vincent Lê speaking.

evidence.passage: Can I just say on that: I think that’s a really good way of structuring this.
evidence.note: Nick Land speaking.

evidence.passage: I totally agree with this thing that, okay, the natural selection mechanism is ultimately the intelligent mechanism.
evidence.note: Nick Land speaking.

records.statement: Taylor's review of 2024 reports that Land's Xenosystems posts oppose what Taylor calls “the implied claim” of those Land calls “orthogonalists”, that “values are transcendent in relation to intelligence”, and hold that “Intelligence, to become anything, has to be a value for itself”.

time.note: Post date; an update of 2024-09-17 is shown.

records.qualification: A relay: Taylor's report of Land's posts as collected in the Passage Publishing book Xenosystems, with short quotations of Land. Land's own posts on xenosystems.net (captures reported from 2013 and 2014) could not be read here, so this 2024 relay is the earliest located wording in this group's search, not the date of Land's texts.

evidence.passage: In “Against Orthogonality”, Land identifies “orthogonalists” such as Michael Annisimov (who previously worked at MIRI) as conceiving of “intelligence as an instrument, directed towards the realization of values that originate externally”. He opposes the implied claim that “values are transcendent in relation to intelligence”.
evidence.note: Taylor reporting Land; the inner quotation marks are Land's wording as she quotes it.

evidence.passage: He says that “Intelligence, to become anything, has to be a value for itself”; intelligence and volition are inter-twined.
evidence.note: Taylor reporting Land's post 'More thought'.

evidence.passage: He concludes: “Whatever we want (consistently) leads through Pythia. Thus, what we really want, is Pythia.”
evidence.note: Taylor reporting Land's post 'Will-to-Think'; the passage concerns what 'we' want, which Taylor glosses as 'regarding humans, not hypothetical VNM superintelligences'; W07 rests on the two preceding passages.

records.statement: Taylor's review of 2024 states that she rejects orthogonality “as stated by Bostrom” and is “inclined to agree” with Land that struggle toward intelligence optimization is “immanently ‘good’”, while finding his “Stupid Monsters” argument not strong against the theoretical possibility of a “VNM paperclipper”.

time.note: Post date; an update of 2024-09-17 is shown.

records.missing: Taylor rejects a formulation of orthogonality and partly agrees with Land, but also holds that agents separating fact from value remain theoretically possible; she does not state that the increase of intelligence is the end that advanced machine intelligence pursues or should pursue.
records.qualification: Records the reviewer's own qualified positions in 2024, including her disagreement with one of Land's arguments.

evidence.locator: Introductory section, paragraph beginning 'I have complex thoughts'
evidence.passage: And, after thinking about it more, I think orthogonality is a bad metaphor and I reject it as stated by Bostrom, for technical reasons I’ll get to.

evidence.locator: Section 'Orthogonality versus Will-to-Think', paragraph on 'Intelligence and the Good'
evidence.passage: “Even the dimmest, most confused struggle in the direction of intelligence optimization is immanently ‘good’ (self-improving). If it wasn’t we might as well all give up now”. I’m currently inclined to agree.
evidence.note: The inner quotation is Land's wording as Taylor quotes it; the last sentence is Taylor's.

evidence.passage: I don’t find this to be a strong argument against the theoretical possibility of a VNM paperclipper, to be clear.
evidence.note: Taylor's disagreement with Land's 'Stupid Monsters' argument.

records.statement: Alexander's post “Meditations On Moloch” of 2014 names Nick Land and states that Land “missed the very last turn, the one marked ORTHOGONALITY THESIS”.

engagement.rationale: The passage names the orthogonality thesis, of which W07 is the contrary, as the point at which Land's reasoning goes wrong, without giving in that passage an argument against W07's premise.

records.qualification: Records the post's naming of the orthogonality thesis against Land; the same section's account of Land's views on other subjects is not recorded. Earliest located among contesting W07 texts in this group's search.

evidence.locator: Section V, paragraph beginning 'That person will not be Nick Land'
evidence.passage: I have such mixed feelings about Nick Land. On the grail quest for the True Futurology, he has gone 99.9% of the path and then missed the very last turn, the one marked ORTHOGONALITY THESIS.

records.statement: Negarestani, in his published conversation with Mackay of 2018, states that disconnecting intelligence from rational agenthood risks “rationalizing nature as intelligence” and that Land “mistakes rational agenthood with a perspectival phenomenal self”.

claimed.note: The standfirst describes the text as an edited and expanded version of a conversation at a book launch in New York in November 2018; the conversation does not date the published wording.

engagement.rationale: Disputes the premise that intelligence can be non-agentic, on which a view of capitalism as an intelligence without agents depends.

records.qualification: Records Negarestani's stated disagreement in the published conversation; the rest of the same answer, which sets a non-agentic view of capitalism against Land's political writing, is not recorded. Earliest located among contesting W06 texts in this group's search.

evidence.locator: Negarestani's answer to the question 'what does it mean to be on the side of intelligence?'
evidence.passage: Nick mistakes rational agenthood with a perspectival phenomenal self (much like eliminativists) that can be explained away by some physical law, but the minded self is a-perspectival.
evidence.note: Reza Negarestani speaking.

evidence.passage: In disconnecting the concept of intelligence from rational agenthood, we run the risk of rationalizing nature as intelligence, or even as an intelligent design.

records.statement: The LessWrong post “Nick Land has no theory of AI, just a theory of capitalism” of 2026 states that calling AI “capitalism” or “capitalist” is “neither a sufficient nor useful descriptor” and that Land “cannot conceptualize plurality and multiplicity in artificial intelligence”.

engagement.rationale: Disputes that identifying AI with capitalism describes AI adequately, arguing that the identification leaves no room for a plurality of artificial intelligences.

records.qualification: Records the post's argument; replies under the post dispute its reading of Land, and its author writes in a comment of 14 October 2026, “I am taking my lumps here and they are deserved. I could have engaged more deeply”.

evidence.passage: Calling AI “capitalism” or “capitalist” is neither a sufficient nor useful descriptor and leaves us mired in centuries-long capitalism debates.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Land has not updated his beliefs'
evidence.passage: Land has not updated his beliefs with advances in AI. Most damningly, he cannot conceptualize plurality and multiplicity in artificial intelligence.

searchLog.searched: Read Land's 'Circuitries' in the scanned Pli 4 volume (1992, journal's PDF, pp. 217–235, all pages viewed), 'Meltdown' in the CCRU web copy, 'Hypervirus' (Urbanomic's PDF of the Fanged Noumena chapter), 'Mechanomics' (Pli 7, 1998), the Hyperstition blog's monthly archives 2004–2008 (all posts signed 'Nick Land' and, for subject terms, those signed 'Old Nick'), Land's 2014 Incredible Machines remarks and Lê's 2026 conversations with Land. Web searches (discovery only) for Land texts on AI, capital and acceleration.
searchLog.earliestNote: 'Circuitries' (Pli 4, October 1992) is the earliest located W01 articulation in this group: it states a horizon of 'a few decades' for artificial intelligences surpassing biological ones and the end of human dominion of terrestrial culture. Its evidence is paraphrase because the scan has no text layer. 'Meltdown' bears on W01 but names capital and a 'meltdown singularity' rather than machine intelligence. The dataset's Moravec records (1979, 1989) are on A1, A3, A4, A5 and are not re-recorded.

searchLog.searched: As for W01; read Circuitries pp. 217–235 for statements valuing the succession.
searchLog.earliestNote: No articulation located. 'Circuitries' (1992) bears on W02 (the 'high road to thinking' through a becoming inhuman of cognition; resistance to the side-lining of human intelligence described as phobic) but does not state that succession is acceptable or desirable in those words.

searchLog.searched: Grepped the retrieved Land texts (Meltdown, Hypervirus, Miserablism post, 2014 remarks, 2026 conversations) for orders-of-magnitude comparisons; read Circuitries pages.
searchLog.earliestNote: Nothing recorded. The Miserablism post's 'a new plane of intelligence, vast beyond human anticipation' (2007) gives no factor or comparison of the kind W05 requires; Circuitries' comparison of human brains to 'mediaeval villages' concerns the setting of thought, not a measured gap.

searchLog.searched: Land texts as above; Lê's Substack archive (API listing of all posts to Oct 2026; read Parts 1–2 of the conversation, Part 3 is paywalled, and the opening of 'Capitalism is AI, AI is Capitalism'); Urbanomic's Fanged Noumena and #Accelerate pages, chapter pages and documents list (found Negarestani and Mackay, 'Reengineering Philosophy', 2018); LessWrong/GreaterWrong posts naming Land; Spike Art Magazine (discovery only).
searchLog.earliestNote: Earliest located W06 articulation with a dated wording: Land's remarks at the Incredible Machines conference (delivered 8 March 2014; transcript posted 10 March 2014), 'the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence'. The Hyperstition post 'Critique of Transcendental Miserablism' (15 January 2007, signed 'Old Nick'; title matches a Fanged Noumena chapter by Land) is recorded as bearing on W06: it speaks of capitalism creating 'a new plane of intelligence' but does not call that intelligence machine or artificial. Correction, 2026-10-31: the 2007 post was previously given the earliest-located role. 'Meltdown' articulates W06 but is read only in an undated CCRU web copy (the CCRU dates Abstract Culture swarm 1 'Winter, 1997'), so it cannot be earliest located. 'Circuitries' (1992) bears on W06. Lê's post of 2026 dates 'Machinic Desire' to 1993 and quotes a W06 passage from it ('an invasion from the future by an artificial intelligent space'); the essay itself (Textual Practice, 1993; Fanged Noumena, 2011) was not retrievable in a copy by the author or publisher. If it is read, it is likely to become the earliest located W06 text. Contesting: Negarestani and Mackay (2018) is the earliest located; jacob (2026) is later.

searchLog.searched: Land's Xenosystems posts ('Against Orthogonality', 'Will-to-Think', 'Pythia Unbound', 'Stupid Monsters', 'Hell-Baked', 'What is Intelligence?', 'Intelligence and the Good', 'More thought', 'Optimize for Intelligence'): xenosystems.net now serves another author's blog and old post addresses return 404; captures listed in retrievalFailures. searchLog.earliestNote: The only W07 articulation recorded is a relay: Taylor's 2024 review, quoting Land's posts. The posts themselves have Internet Archive captures from 2013-07-04 ('What is Intelligence?'), 2013-09-14 ('Pythia Unbound'), 2013-10-28 ('Against Orthogonality') and 2014-09-17 ('Will-to-Think'); if the cross-family checker can open them, the earliest located W07 text is likely to move to 2013. Alexander's 'Meditations On Moloch' (30 July 2014) names Land and the orthogonality thesis against him and is the earliest located contesting text here. W07 sits beside Y02 and the risk-debate pack's R01 (orthogonality); no text here is recorded on those.

openQuestions.question: Hyperstition posts signed 'Old Nick' (2006–2008) include 'Sense and Singularity' (17 July 2007: 'Rigorously conceived Singularity is Intelligence Catastrophe … aka Planetary Meltdown, the Immanent Limit of Capitalism') and 'Yudkowsky' (11 June 2007, quoting 'Staring into the Singularity'). Can they be recorded as Land's?
openQuestions.recommended: Only if a source by Land or a publisher attributes them to him. The Miserablism post is recorded under its signature, with the Fanged Noumena chapter title noted; the others are left out.

openQuestions.question: Should 'Meltdown' be dated by the CCRU's 'Winter, 1997' date for Abstract Culture swarm 1, with the wording attested only from retrieval?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the 1997 work date with the attested note; ask the cross-family checker to open the 2004 capture, and correct if Fanged Noumena's list of sources (not read) gives another date.

openQuestions.question: Hazard note on 'Meltdown': the text contains second-person fiction of killing 'Turing cops' and the line that 'All political institutions are cyberian military targets'. Is the hazard note warranted?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it as a precaution; nothing from those passages is quoted.

openQuestions.question: Register of 'Meltdown': the W06 passage is framed 'The story goes like this', and other sections of the text are second-person fiction. Should the whole text carry one register?
openQuestions.recommended: All four Meltdown records (W01, W06, W08, W09) are labelled nonfiction: the quoted passages are expository or a narrative framing of a compressed history. The second-person fiction sections are noted in the W06 qualification and not quoted.

openQuestions.question: Circuitries evidence is paraphrase from page images. Should an OCR of the journal's scan be added to the cache so that quotations can be checked mechanically?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, if an OCR tool becomes available; then replace the paraphrases with short quotations (the p. 219 passage on 'a few decades' especially).

openQuestions.question: Mackay and Avanessian's #Accelerate introduction (2014) may also be recorded by the accelerationist-texts group.
